title: Stigmatization campaign since the Robertson Panel

tellings.quote: Well, remember this this whole stigmatization has been an 80-year campaign and it's been very effective and wellunded. It started after the Robertson panel

The "debunking" aim would result in reduction in public interest in "flying saucers" which today evokes a strong psychological reaction. This education could be accomplished by mass media such as television, motion pictures, and popular articles.

a. That the national security agencies take immediate steps to strip the Unidentified Flying Objects of the special status they have been given and the aura of mystery they have unfortunately acquired;

plain: The stigma around UFOs is said to be an eighty-year campaign, "very effective and well funded," that began with the Robertson Panel, a group of scientists the CIA convened in January 1953. A retired Navy admiral named Tim Gallaudet tells Michels this, which would mean public ridicule of the subject was planned. The panel's report, dated 16 February 1953, does call for a "debunking" aim to reduce public interest in "flying saucers" through "television, motion pictures, and popular articles," and urges agencies to "strip the Unidentified Flying Objects of the special status they have been given and the aura of mystery they have unfortunately acquired."
